structure.heading: Make-versus-Buy Decision, Preferred Supplier Selection Criteria, and Contracting Approach
text_content: **Make-versus-Buy Decision, Preferred Supplier Selection Criteria, and Contracting Approach**

L2 service desk and end-user device support, effective 2026-01-01. Transition planning commences Q3 2025 with knowledge transfer and SOC integration to align SLAs to IT managed services baselines. This split preserves advanced incident response and security control while reducing cost and improving responsiveness for high-volume user support.

Preferred supplier selection will be driven by weighted criteria: Total Cost of Ownership 35%, Service Performance 25%, Security & Compliance 20%, Scalability 10%, and ESG 10%. Evaluation will include financial models, performance scorecards, security certifications (ISO 27001, SOC 2), scalability proof points, and ESG reporting. Finalists will undergo reference checks, technical pilots, and a commercial bid against the weighted scoring matrix.

The contracting approach is to execute a 36-month Master Services Agreement with two optional 12-month renewals and include service credits capped at 10% of monthly fees. The MSA will specify KPIs, governance forums, change control, transition and exit terms, and data protection obligations. Pricing will include defined TCO elements and periodic review mechanisms.

structure.heading: Category Spend Analysis and Demand Baseline for Enterprise IT Managed Services
text_content: **Category Spend Analysis and Demand Baseline for Enterprise IT Managed Services**

FY2025 total Enterprise IT Managed Services spend is $48.6M across 312 purchase orders, averaging about $155,800 per PO. This consolidated baseline underpins demand normalization and budget alignment, and will be used for sourcing scenario modeling, PO-level outlier detection, and prioritization of high-volume service lines for targeted negotiation and efficiency initiatives consistently across enterprise business units.

The supplier concentration is elevated: Apex Managed Services, NorthBridge IT, and CloudOps Partners account for 71% of FY2025 spend. This concentration creates leverage for consolidated negotiations and supplier risk that requires mitigation. Actions include targeted performance KPIs, tiered sourcing strategies, contingency agreements, and scheduled contract reviews to reduce single-vendor exposure while preserving economies of scale.

From 2024-01-01 to 2025-12-31, demand is 62% run-the-business operations and 38% project-based services. Operational services require SLA-driven, OPEX-friendly contracts with continuous performance metrics; project services require fixed-scope SOWs, milestone billnig, and modular change control. Sourcing must effectively align commercial vehicles to these distinct demand profiles.
